cs_qualification.expander_read_cannot_corrupt_sensor: a sensor armed (GP3 low) during an expander or OLED frame is deselected by BUS_BUSY 18.8 ns after the frame's chip select falls, 31.2 ns before its first clock (the frame is lost, nothing is decoded or driven)
firmware_sequence: 0. UI power-up: wait >= 30 ms (OLED rule, U12); expander at reset has every GP an input, pulled high: both devices deselected; write OLAT bits 3 and 7 = 1 BEFORE writing IODIR bits 3 and 7 = 0 (OLAT resets to 0 and would drive the pins low).

1. Expander device configuration for these accesses: mode 0, <= 5 MHz, cs_ena_posttrans >= 3 bit cycles (CS_EXP# stays low >= 600 ns after the last clock, so the GP output has settled before CS_EXP# rises).
2. Lock the whole SPI bus (OLED chunk transfers cannot interleave).
3. Write OLAT with GP3 low (select request). CS_EXP# and CS_OLED# are idle high after the write.

4. Wait >= 1 us. Clock exactly 32 bits (TMAG5170) or 16 bits (TMP122) with NO hardware chip select (spics_io_num = -1): CS_EXP# and CS_OLED# stay high, so the gate holds the selection. SCK <= 5 MHz (1 MHz first; 2.5 MHz recommended cap).
5. Wait >= 1 us. Write OLAT with GP3 high (release). The first CS_EXP# edge deselects the sensor before the first expander clock.
6. Unlock the bus. Never leave GP3 or GP7 low outside steps 3-5; never set both low.
7. Each sensor frame needs its own select/release pair (CS must toggle between 32-clock frames: SBASAF4 p.28).
cs_qualification.function: CS_dev# = GPx OR NAND(CS_EXP#, CS_OLED#); selected only when GPx = 0 AND CS_EXP# = 1 AND CS_OLED# = 1
